Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Helidon accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.3 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions.

The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute is empty, whitespace-only or non-numeric, or when such dimensions come from a WSDL definition. Four bytes of unrelated heap data can then be used as an integer key in the decoded array. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a crafted request to a SoapServer endpoint, and a malicious SOAP server with a response to SoapClient. Heap memory is disclosed only if the application returns or otherwise exposes the decoded array.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction.

The PHP CGI binary (php-cgi), in CGI and FastCGI mode with cgi.fix_pathinfo enabled (the default), can perform an out-of-bounds read and write when the path removed from SCRIPT_FILENAME or PATH_TRANSLATED is longer than the supplied PATH_INFO, or when PATH_INFO is empty. This requires a web server mapping that passes such inconsistent values, or a FastCGI listener reachable by untrusted clients. An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the process, may obtain process memory if the application exposes PATH_INFO or PATH_TRANSLATED, and may corrupt memory. PHP-FPM and the Apache module are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

SOAP use-after-free when processing DTD entity references.

The SOAP extension frees the document type definition (DTD) of a parsed XML document while attribute values can still refer to entities it owns, and can then read freed memory. Removing the DTD also bypasses the SOAP server's rejection of documents that contain one. An unauthenticated remote attacker who can send a crafted request to a SOAP endpoint, or who controls a WSDL or schema document loaded by the application, can crash the PHP process and cause denial of service. Memory disclosure and code execution have not been confirmed.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Vulnerability in the Helidon product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: helidon-security-jwt).  Supported versions that are affected are 3.0.0-3.2.22. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Helidon.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Helidon accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Helidon accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.9 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N).

PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields.

The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worker without escaping them for the HTML, XML or JSON format. When the status endpoint is enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker can store markup in a worker's scoreboard entry with an ordinary request, for example through the username of an HTTP Basic authentication header that the web server forwards to PHP-FPM, or through the script filename where the attacker can influence it. When a user views the full status page as HTML, the injected JavaScript runs in the origin of that page. The attacker does not need access to the status endpoint. Malformed XML or JSON output can also disrupt monitoring tools.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the Nixpacks publishDirectory build setting accepts shell metacharacters and is interpolated into a docker cp command executed through child_process.exec. An authenticated user with access to an application can execute arbitrary commands on the Dokploy host when triggering a Nixpacks deployment, leading to host compromise through the privileged Docker environment. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Enterprise Manager Base Platform product of Oracle Enterprise Manager (component: Agent Next Gen).  Supported versions that are affected are 13.5 and  24.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Enterprise Manager Base Platform executes to compromise Oracle Enterprise Manager Base Platform.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Enterprise Manager Base Platform accessible data as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Enterprise Manager Base Platform accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.1 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N).

Mareforma is a local verification layer for AI-assisted research. From 0.3.0 until 0.3.8, restore logic in mareforma/db/restore.py derives transparency_logged from the unsigned rekor.uuid field inside signature_bundle without requiring a verified claim-bound rekor_inclusions entry, so an attacker who modifies claims.toml can falsely make a claim eligible for REPLICATED convergence. The same logic resets signed claims in non-Rekor graphs from transparency_logged 1 to 0 after restore, permanently preventing convergence because no Rekor refresh is configured. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.8.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Business Process Management Suite product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Human workflow 11g+).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Business Process Management Suite.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Business Process Management Suite, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Business Process Management Suite accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Business Process Management Suite accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.4 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N).

A vulnerability was identified in Directus up to 12.7.0. This issue affects the function AuthenticationService.refresh of the file api/src/services/authentication.ts of the component Authentication Service. Such manipulation leads to session expiration. The attack can be launched remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

storyblok-backup is an npx CLI tool to create backups of a Storyblok space and restore individual resources. Prior to 0.7.1, the writeJson function used the editable Storyblok component name field as a filename without path containment. A person with component-management access in a Storyblok space could store a component name containing path traversal sequences; when another user later ran a backup for that space, the stored name escaped the configured backup directory and caused a JSON file to be written outside it on the backup host. Depending on the path chosen and the backup process's permissions, this could overwrite existing files at attacker-chosen locations. The vulnerability is specific to components: stories and datasources use numeric identifiers, and asset names are reduced to a final path segment. This issue is fixed in version 0.7.1.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Planning product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Security).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Planning.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Hyperion Planning accessible data as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Hyperion Planning accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.9 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N).

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, ToolboxSettings.parse builds a deeply nested attacker-controlled settings tree iteratively, but the later public helpers to_settings_string, remove_blanks, add_default_fields, sort_fields, and add_blank_lines recursively traverse that tree without a depth bound. Invoking any of those helpers on input nested beyond the interpreter recursion limit can raise RecursionError and abort the operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Common Security).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via SSH to compromise Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N).

Axon is an agent-agnostic context engine that gives AI coding agents continuous memory across sessions, tools, and machines. Prior to 0.1.1, rtk-install in src/axon/context/rtk_bootstrap.py uses _http_download() to fetch a prebuilt rtkx release archive and _extract_binary() to mark it executable, after which compress_text_with_rtk() invokes it without verifying a checksum, signature, or build attestation. If the sammyjdev/rtkx release pipeline or maintainer release credentials are compromised, an attacker can supply a modified binary that executes with the Axon process privileges when a user installs or automatically bootstraps rtkx. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.1.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Analytics (component: Installation).  Supported versions that are affected are 8.2.0.0.0, 12.2.1.4.0 and  26.01.0.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition executes to compromise Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.8 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers. Prior to 2.8.0, parse_arguments() passes the caller-controlled return_type parameter for config/core/get_value, config/providers/get_value, and config/players/get_value to parse_value() and Python eval() when resolving type parameters in music_assistant/helpers/api.py. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reach these commands through the WebSocket /ws endpoint or the REST JSON-RPC /api endpoint, causing arbitrary Python code to run with the Music Assistant server process privileges before command-handler validation, even if the request later fails. A default installation requires no special configuration, and compromise can expose secrets and configuration, alter library data, and control the application container. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Analytics (component: Platform Security).  Supported versions that are affected are 8.2.0.0.0, 12.2.1.4.0 and  26.01.0.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.8 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).

A vulnerability was detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. Affected by this issue is the function json_load_lock of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi of the component Jsonstatus. The manipulation of the argument usefile results in stack-based buffer overflow. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 can resolve this issue. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2 the current request details debug endpoint exposed authentication headers and session cookies

Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, the Open OnDemand dashboard includes noVNC passwords in query parameters generated by apps/dashboard/app/helpers/batch_connect/sessions_helper.rb and apps/dashboard/app/views/batch_connect/sessions/connections/_novnc.html.erb. The server records those query strings in per-user PUN access logs, and insufficiently protected log directories can allow another local user to recover and replay a launch URL. Replaying the credential grants access to the running remote desktop and can result in horizontal or vertical privilege escalation according to the privileges of the desktop owner. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 app widgets could perform API requests on behalf of viewing users without their consent

PHPGurukul Beauty Parlour Management System V1.1 uses a non-cryptographic function to generate security-sensitive appointment and invoice identifiers. The identifiers are generated within a restricted numeric range and are subsequently used in record lookup operations. This implementation exposes the application to identifier prediction or guessing attacks under conditions where the identifiers are relied upon as a security boundary.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 improper authorization allowed read-only users to change issue fields via agile boards

mini-snmpd is a minimal SNMP agent implementation. Prior to 1.7, the ASN.1 BER parser in protocol.c does not verify that an attacker-controlled field length is no greater than the remaining packet size before decode_str(), decode_oid(), and decode_ptr() evaluate size - len + 1. When len exceeds size, unsigned size_t arithmetic wraps and bypasses the bounds check, allowing the decoder to read beyond the 2048-byte packet buffer. Parsing occurs before the SNMP community string is checked, so a remote unauthenticated attacker can send one crafted request to UDP port 161 to crash the process and potentially disclose adjacent heap memory. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.
temporary redacted

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an authenticated user can supply a user-controlled, array-valued GPG key identifier to the key deletion action. Validate::string() filters HTML characters but not shell metacharacters. The user-controlled identifier reaches the delete action without shell-safe encoding. controllers/Gpg.php contains the vulnerable deletion path. Process::execute() passes the command string through proc_open() and /bin/sh -c, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web/PHP process. This can expose secrets or poison packages. Authentication is required, but the advisory makes an administrator-only restriction conditional on the intended access policy and does not establish an administrator role as a prerequisite. Fixed in 5.13.3.

A flaw has been found in elunez eladmin up to 2.7. Affected by this vulnerability is the function SqlUtils.sanitizeJdcUrl of the component JDBC URL Sanitization. Executing a manipulation can lead to improper input validation. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 private issue summaries and descriptions could be read via agile board queries for archived projects

Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in Conditional_execute() because SetupConditional() stores a BIFS decoder pointer that gf_sm_load_run_isom() later frees without clearing. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with a BIFS Conditional node processed with -nstatx to crash MP4Box and potentially corrupt the heap.

Attendize through 2.8.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in EventOrdersController::postCancelOrder() that allows authenticated organisers to cancel attendees belonging to other accounts' events. Attackers can cancel one of their own orders while supplying foreign attendee IDs, which Attendee::findFromSelection() loads unfiltered, invalidating tickets for any event on the installation.
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19766 helpdesk email attachments were sent to CC recipients without a visibility check

Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting services. Prior to 1.5.7, the HasConfirmation trait in app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php, included by app/Livewire/Component.php across 36 client-facing Livewire components, exposed executeConfirmedAction as a public action that invoked any component method accepted by method_exists. The action could call inherited InteractsWithProperties::fill(), whose data_set() writes arbitrary public properties, including state marked with #[Locked] and dotted paths into hydrated Eloquent models. Depending on the methods and properties exposed by an individual component, an unauthenticated caller could use this path to bypass intended authorization and modify server-side state intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.7.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in xmt_parse_script_field() that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read via duplicate Script field names with conflicting types. Attackers can craft an XMT file that, when imported with MP4Box, causes gf_sg_vrml_mf_reset() to treat a single-value field as multi-value, crashing the application.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_node_try_destroy because Conditional node commands keep raw pointers to target nodes freed by gf_sg_reset(). Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene processed with -info or -add to trigger heap use-after-free, crashing the process and corrupting heap memory.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the CCG lexicon parser's matchBrackets and augParseCategory functions recursively process nested parenthesized categories without a depth bound. An attacker-controlled lexicon string with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through nltk.ccg.lexicon.fromstring and terminate the parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_node_try_destroy that allows attackers to crash MP4Box by supplying crafted XMT scene files. Commands created inside a PROTO scope keep a raw pointer to a freed prototype sub-scene graph, which is read during teardown, causing denial of service.

Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information, Insufficiently Protected Credentials vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android (Address book sync, Heartbeat sync loop modules) allows Sniffing Attacks.

The client places the preset address-book password verbatim into the heartbeat sync JSON body (src/hbbs_http/sync.rs). Over an intact HTTPS session it is not exposed in transit, but it is a reusable shared secret rather than a zero-knowledge proof, so it is recovered by any party that becomes the API endpoint - under the re-homed/rogue API server (CVE-2026-30797) - and the leaked credential then authorizes the server-side address book.

This vulnerability is associated with program files src/hbbs_http/sync.rs and program routines heartbeat sync body builder (emits preset-address-book-password).

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.8. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. A crafted pickle can invoke recfromtxt to read a local file or open_memmap to create or truncate an attacker-selected file when a victim loads an untrusted model. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in DoWriteMeta() in src/isomedia/isom_store.c that allows attackers to crash MP4Box via crafted files. Attackers can supply an ISOBMFF file with a meta box containing an iloc entry but no dref box, crashing MP4Box during rewrite operations like -unhint.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the semantic-logic read_type parser recursively processes both halves of nested complex type strings without applying LogicParser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH. An attacker-controlled type string or signature with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through Type.fromstring or type-checking entry points and abort the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

obsidian-sync-mcp is an MCP server that gives AI agents access to Obsidian vaults. Prior to 0.5.7, deployments running without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN install no serverOptions.authenticate check for the HTTP /mcp endpoint, so requests are dispatched without validating the Host or Origin headers. A malicious website visited by the operator can use DNS rebinding to reach loopback, LAN, VPN, or container-published addresses, or directly issue a cross-origin request to loopback, and invoke the MCP tool surface to read, create, overwrite, delete, or move vault notes. Deployments using MCP_AUTH_TOKEN are not affected because browsers do not attach the bearer token. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.7.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in ReportRun::generateAdvFilterSql() that allows authenticated low-privileged users to inject SQL via the bw comparator. Attackers can send a crafted advanced_filter parameter containing a single quote to the Reports getRecordsCount action to break out of BETWEEN literals and extract database contents.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to inject SQL through the k (does not contain) comparator in list view search_params. Attackers can send crafted search_params to the ListAjax getRecordsCount mode, breaking out of the unescaped NOT LIKE clause to extract database contents via boolean or time-based techniques.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one for which the header was intended. That unintended host can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or other confidential values. Authorization headers are never forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH URL path component as a single argument when constructing remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the intended path argument and cause arbitrary command execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH URL is configured and the remote host either does not support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

A vulnerability was detected in SEO Panel 6.0.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file controllers/siteauditor.ctrl.php of the component Site Auditor. Performing a manipulation of the argument order_col/order_val results in sql injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 7.0.0 will fix this issue. The patch is named 389783b5d8235f5637f4e4587f524b5fef07864d. The affected component should be upgraded.

A security flaw has been discovered in SourceCodester Simple Form Builder Web App 1.0. The impacted element is the function save_form of the file /classes/Forms.php. Performing a manipulation of the argument form_code/form_data results in code injection. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A vulnerability was determined in SourceCodester Student Project Allocation and Management System 1.0. Affected is an unknown function of the file /login.php of the component Login Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument username/password can lead to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.
vp: student project allocation and management system

cves.d: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that occurs when AVERAGE and PAETH filters process zero-width PNG images. A malicious multiplayer server can supply a crafted texture pack URL or player skin to write past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing connecting clients.

MP4v2 through 2.1.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in MP4RtpHintTrack::GetPayload() in src/rtphint.cpp that passes an unchecked rtpmap value to strchr(). Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file whose RTP hint track has a corrupted hinf atom to crash mp4info or applications calling MP4GetHintTrackRtpPayload().

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in DynamiApps Frontend Admin by DynamiApps acf-frontend-form-element allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Frontend Admin by DynamiApps: from n/a through 3.30.2.

Daptin is a GraphQL/JSON-API headless CMS. From 0.11.4 until 0.12.30, the generic GET /yjs/:documentName WebSocket route in InitializeYjsResources requires a session but does not authorize the database resource selected by a typename.referenceId.columnName room name. The YJS initial-content provider then reads the selected file.* column without CanRead or CanUpdate checks, and bidirectional synchronization allows a low-privileged authenticated user to read or modify restricted row content. Unauthenticated requests are rejected, and standalone non-canonical room names remain shared-by-name rooms. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The authentication bypass requires submitting the JSON boolean `true` as the `prod_key_random_id` value, which coerces against any non-empty stored secret so that the loose `!=` comparison evaluates to false, skipping the rejection branch entirely without knowledge of the secret.

The Slimbox Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'el.title (HTML-decoded title attribute of a stored <a rel^=lightbox> element)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a companion plugin such as bbPress that permits low-privileged users to store anchor elements with arbitrary title and rel attributes, as WordPress core comment handling does not preserve rel on anchor tags by default.

Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows collaborators with write access to push to protected branches by merging pull requests. Because MergePullRequest skips branch protection checks and PullRequest.Merge omits hook environment variables, attackers can merge commits into branches restricted to allowlisted users.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - IDOR in backend data export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The backend export did not correctly verify permissions for the exported form, allowing backend users to export data of forms they are not authorized to access.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Input placeholders in SQL field statements were inserted without quoting in the public reload task, allowing unauthenticated SQL injection in read queries.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Code injection via calculation formulas in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Calculation field formulas were executed using PHP eval() without validating their content, allowing backend users with field edit permissions to execute arbitrary PHP code.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, the public Relation API lacks an access-control filter. Unauthenticated users can query its REST endpoints and GraphQL endpoints to discover metadata about unpublished, draft, and viewless content. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Open redirect on invalid form submission in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The return parameter of an invalid form submission was not validated, allowing redirects to external sites.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 3.7.0 before 3.30.5 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in parseAttributes and parseShortcodeAttributes that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through quadratic backtracking. Attackers can supply Markdown with long crafted attribute strings parsed by createBlockMarkdownSpec, createAtomBlockMarkdownSpec or createInlineMarkdownSpec to stall browser pages or server processes.
Ruby before 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10 has a heap-based buffer overflow during case conversion. One byte can be written outside a buffer for, for example, ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an arbitrary file upload attack due to insufficient file type validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file deletion via path traversal in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The delete and rename tasks of the CSS editor lacked authorization checks, CSRF protection and path validation, allowing backend users to delete files outside the CSS directory.

Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution'), Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk, hbb_common on Windows, MacOS, Linux (Password security module, config encryption, machine UID modules) allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data. This vulnerability is associated with program files hbb_common/src/password_security.Rs, hbb_common/src/config.Rs, hbb_common/src/lib.Rs (get_uuid), machine-uid/src/lib.Rs and program routines symmetric_crypt(), encrypt_str_or_original(), decrypt_str_or_original(), get_uuid(), get_machine_id().

This issue affects RustDesk Client: through 1.4.5. NOTE: some third parties have indicated that these details do not align with the Supplier's statements.

Goproxy before 1.9.4 contains a weak key generation vulnerability in NewCounterEncryptorRandFromKey that derives RSA and Ed25519 leaf certificate private keys from public data due to misuse of hash.Sum. Attackers with the CA certificate and one observed leaf certificate can regenerate that host's leaf private key and impersonate the host to clients trusting the proxy CA.

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Arbitrary file write leading to remote code execution in CSS editor in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The CSS editor did not restrict file names, extensions and paths of created and saved files, allowing privileged backend users to write arbitrary PHP files.

HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 functions cram_xpack_decode_char and cram_xrle_decode_char do not validate that attacker-controlled decode sizes remain within their expanded input arrays. Crafted CRAM data can therefore make either decoder read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially disclosing process-state information or crashing the process through invalid memory access. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Path traversal in file upload in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - File names of uploads were not reduced to their base name when the option to retain original file names was enabled, potentially allowing files to be written outside the upload directory.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin/support.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the module parameter. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to run script in the admin panel, reading CSRF tokens and changing shop settings.

HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM BETA decoder functions cram_beta_decode_long, cram_beta_decode_int, and cram_beta_decode_char, and the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK functions cram_xpack_decode_long and cram_xpack_decode_int, have bounds-checking flaws caused by integer overflow after a multiplication. The resulting incorrect bounds check can allow decoding to read beyond the supplied input buffer, potentially leaking process-state information or crashing the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

node-soap before 1.14.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in WSDL.xmlToObject that allows unauthenticated attackers to pollute Object.prototype via an XML element with id="__proto__". Attackers can send a single crafted SOAP request to a soap.listen() server, or return a malicious response to a client, causing all subsequent SOAP parsing to fail until process restart.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Access restriction bypass for form submissions in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Form submissions did not check the access level of the form, allowing guests to submit forms restricted to specific user groups.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to move other forms' shared assets by supplying their URLs in file upload fields. Attackers can submit a public form with another form's cover or logo URL, causing Storage::move() to relocate it into submissions and break that asset.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated verification mail amplification in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The verification mail task accepted arbitrary form IDs and recipients without rate limiting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to trigger mass verification mails and database entries.

A vulnerability in rustdesk-client RustDesk Client rustdesk-client on Windows, MacOS, Linux, iOS, Android, WebClient (Strategy sync, HTTP API client, config options engine modules) allows Application API Message Manipulation via Man-in-the-Middle.

 This vulnerability is associated with program files src/hbbs_http/sync.Rs, hbb_common/src/config.Rs and program routines Strategy merge loop in sync.Rs, Config::set_options().

This vulnerability is associated with program routines Config export/generation routines.

This issue affects RustDesk Server Pro: through 1.7.5. NOTE: the Supplier's position is that this is not a vulnerability.

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing SQL statement permission check in form import and field creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The core.create.sql.statement permission was not enforced when importing forms or creating new fields, allowing backend users without this permission to store arbitrary SQL statements.

OFFIS DCMTK 3.5.4 through 3.7.1 contains an integer overflow in DJCodecEncoder::encodeTrueLossless size checks that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read. Attackers can supply a crafted DICOM file with large Columns, Rows and SamplesPerPixel values that, when compressed with true-lossless JPEG, crashes the application.

Quasar before 2.35.3 contains a DOM clobbering vulnerability that allows attackers to break native wrapper detection by injecting HTML elements named Capacitor, cordova, or StatusBar. Attackers can place markup such as a div with id Capacitor into server-rendered or pre-rendered HTML so app.use(Quasar) throws and the application never mounts, or openURL() and AddressbarColor.set() throw.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, LoginFormAuthenticator accepts unsafe destinations for the login success redirect and login failure redirect. An attacker can direct a user to an attacker-controlled domain after authentication succeeds or fails, enabling phishing and potential token theft. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.5, the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints validate only a submitted URL before fetching it server-side. The fetchers then follow redirects without revalidating each destination, allowing an authenticated user to bypass UrlSafetyChecker and cause the server to request internal or cloud-metadata addresses. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.5.

Manyfold 0.124.0 before 0.154.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to make the instance fetch internal URLs by supplying malicious ActivityPub actor icon.url and image.url fields. Attackers can deliver Create or Update activities to the inbox, causing the Shrine remote_url plugin to request internal or cloud metadata hosts and store responses as creator avatar or banner attachments.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject iframe attributes via the maxheight parameter of the GET /oembed endpoint. Attackers can supply a single quote in maxheight to inject an onload handler into the returned html, executing script in third-party oEmbed consumers that embed it unsanitized.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and perform unauthorized actions within the context of the application. This is MTLVULN-1877.

Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a file mask bypass vulnerability allowing attackers to upload restricted files via an embedded NUL byte in Upload Link filenames. Attackers can plant a Lua session file with a chosen UID and send a matching UID cookie to execute operating system commands as the service account.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

Frappe is a full-stack web application framework. Prior to 15.108.0 and 16.18.3, the add_comment handler in frappe/templates/includes/comments/comments.py trusts the client-provided comment_by and comment_email fields. A caller can submit chosen identity metadata that is stored with a comment, causing the comment to appear to originate from another name or email address. This issue is fixed in versions 15.108.0 and 16.18.3.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Unauthenticated SQL injection in frontend data view filters in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Sorting, location radius and published filters of the frontend data view were not properly sanitized, allowing SQL injection, partly without authentication.

HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, cram_index_load does not verify that the number of reference sequences in a CRAM .crai index does not exceed the CRAM header reference count. A malformed index can drive unbounded index-array allocation, and when the number of references in the index is within two of INT_MAX, the growth calculation can wrap, read beyond a heap buffer, and use the resulting value as a pointer for an unchecked memory write. Any region query can trigger the flaw, causing denial of service or memory corruption. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Verification mail rate limit reset in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The rate limit for verification mails was reset on every form render, rendering the limit ineffective.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.

When payload encryption is enabled, failure messages and stack traces that temporal-proxy is configured to keep from the upstream Temporal service can reach it in plaintext, where anyone who can read the Workflow's history at the upstream can read them. When the proxy returns a failure to a Worker, it decrypts the failure's encoded attributes and copies the message and stack trace back onto the failure, keeping the attributes. A Worker that sends that failure back through the proxy, as SDKs do when an Activity failure becomes the cause of a Workflow failure, sends the restored text with it, and the proxy forwards the text unchanged because the failure already has encoded attributes. The upstream then stores the text in plaintext beside its encrypted copy. This affects deployments that enable failure encryption in the proxy, and deployments that leave it off while the SDK encodes failure attributes itself. Payloads are not affected. temporal-proxy versions 0.9.0 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in form creation in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.3, 6.0.0-6.2.0 - The createForm task of the form creator did not check the core.create permission, allowing backend users without create permission to create forms.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the unsanitized products_model field. Attackers with product editing permission can store JavaScript that executes in browsers of other administrators, storefront visitors, and customers viewing carts and order history.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an attacker who controls an upstream RPM repository mirrored by a RepoManager instance can provide a package filename through the primary.xml <location href> field; the mirror passes that filename into a shell-interpreted RPM query, allowing shell metacharacters to execute commands as the www-data service account. The target must mirror an upstream repository controlled by the attacker, and the default "Check GPG signatures" option triggers the vulnerable call. The command executes before a later signature-verification failure, so a valid signed package is not required. Fixed in 5.13.3.

falcon-rust is a Rust implementation of the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme. Prior to 0.2.0, the discrete-Gaussian sampler in src/samplerz.rs evaluates approx_exp, ber_exp, and sampler_z acceptance probabilities with FixedPoint64 values having only 32 fractional bits. The scaling in approx_exp quantizes its input and limits relative precision to about 2^-33, below Falcon's required bound, causing reference known-answer vectors to diverge and invalidating the proof assumption that secret-dependent signature and key distributions are negligibly close to the ideal discrete Gaussian. This is a cryptographic-soundness defect and no practical key-recovery attack has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.0.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing authorization and CSRF checks in reset and check-in tasks in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The tasks to reset submitted data and to check in forms lacked authorization checks and CSRF protection.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Stored XSS via SQL field labels in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Labels and values of SQL field options were returned unescaped by the reload task and inserted into the page as HTML, allowing stored XSS if the statement reads user-supplied data.

AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms uses a public hard-coded fallback JWT signing secret from server/config/auth.config.js when ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is unset. An unauthenticated attacker can sign a self-contained token with privileged claims because server/src/auth/auth_jwt.js verifies the signature without reloading the user from the database, and server/src/lib/middleware.js trusts the token's roles and options for authorization. A forged token can therefore be accepted as an administrator session, resulting in authentication bypass and full privileged API access. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing the data indefinitely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by repeatedly initiating streaming requests and disconnecting, exhausting worker threads and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. In 3.10.3 and earlier, DependencyGraph._tree and triples recurse once per dependency edge without a depth bound, and get_cycle_path also lacks a visited-set termination guard. A deeply chained or cyclic attacker-controlled CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency structure can raise RecursionError and abort a parse worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Improper per-form authorization for field management in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Field creation, editing and ordering checked permissions against a user-supplied form ID instead of the form the field belongs to, allowing backend users to manage fields of other forms.

Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 through 1.4.3.3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the catchimage action of /ueditor/net/controller.ashx that only validates the Content-Type header. Unauthenticated attackers can supply a source[] URL like x.jpg?.aspx to retain a malicious extension and write an executable .aspx file for remote code execution. NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.max_depth, min_depth, hypernym_paths, and hypernym_distances recursively follow attacker-controlled corpus pointers without a visited-node set or depth cap. A cyclic or excessively deep hypernym graph can raise RecursionError and terminate traversal APIs and similarity operations that depend on them. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing access check in reload task in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - The public reload task did not check form and field access levels, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve results of SQL field statements of restricted forms.

FineReport 8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files through the resourcepath parameter of the /WebReport/ReportServer endpoint. Attackers can send GET requests with op=chart and cmd=get_geo_json to read sensitive files like privilege.xml and extract admin credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing core.create check in example data generation and BreezingForms import in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.4, 6.0.0-6.2.1 - Example data generation and the BreezingForms import did not check the core.create permission for the affected forms, allowing backend users to create records without permission.

Rocket.Chat versions 0.61.0 before 3.11.4, 3.12.x before 3.12.4 and 3.13.x before 3.13.2 contain a missing authorization vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to read any room's messages via the livechat:loadHistory Meteor method. Attackers can mint a guest token through livechat:registerGuest and send POST requests to /api/v1/method.callAnon with a target rid parameter to retrieve message history without membership checks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2025-02-13.

OTOBO 10.0.1 before 10.0.13 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary URLs to the ExternalURLJump action. Attackers can craft GET requests to /otobo/index.pl?Action=ExternalURLJump with a malicious URL parameter, which the ExternalURLJump.pm module redirects to without an allow-list check, enabling phishing attacks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

cves.d: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.classify.weka.ARFF_Formatter writes attacker-controlled class labels into the Weka ARFF @ATTRIBUTE '-label-' declaration without safely formatting the label tokens. Crafted labels can alter the generated ARFF schema or records, corrupting classifier input and causing integrity loss or processing failure. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode can enforce MCP_TOKEN on /mcp while leaving the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes unauthenticated. An unauthenticated network caller can use /api/connect to replace runtime_url and document_url values and their tokens, reset ServerContext, and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure, causing the server to send Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to that backend. The caller can also use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. This boundary failure does not require explicit insecure no-auth mode and occurs outside normal MCP JSON-RPC tool dispatch. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

TeamPass is a self-hosted collaborative password manager. Prior to 3.2.1.2, the update_folder action in app/sources/folders.queries.php allowed an authenticated, non-read-only user to re-parent a folder without checking whether the target folder or submitted parentId belonged to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. Selecting a personal folder as the new parent passed the personal-folder guard and set personal_folder on the target, transferring the credential subtree into the attacker's accessible space after the next login and hiding it from the organization, including administrators. The change exposed credential labels, logins, URLs, email addresses, and descriptions, while sharekey-protected passwords remained protected; hiding the subtree also denied other users access. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.1.2.

Synway SMG Gateway Management Software builds through 2022-03-15 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the downfile parameter in /down.php. Attackers can send a multipart POST request to /down.php with a traversal path in downfile to retrieve sensitive files like /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to 3.10.3, NLTK ZIP package extraction can write through an existing in-root hardlink whose other link points outside the NLTK data root. A local attacker who can prepare the extraction target can cause a package member write to overwrite an out-of-root file, violating the pathsec containment boundary and affecting integrity and availability. This issues is fixed in version 3.10.4.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered
customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is
decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If
the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the
name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens
the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator
and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are
not affected, because the name is encoded again.

FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed.

This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts.

Security impact:
- Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope.
- Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted.

Affected version: <4.1.0.

Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.

When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace, PHP can read stale values that may refer to freed memory. If a fatal error such as exceeding memory_limit occurs while an application enters such a call, with fatal_error_backtraces enabled (the default) and zend.exception_ignore_args disabled, a remote attacker who controls enough request data to influence memory allocation may cause memory corruption, crash the PHP worker or, with knowledge of memory addresses, execute arbitrary code. php.ini-production enables zend.exception_ignore_args, which prevents this.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
